title: Sling Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.184)
subtitle: Use before slings are used each day and whenever service conditions call for a further check during use.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; mark a whole section N/A when it does not match the sling type.

If any item is marked Defect, remove the sling from service at once (1910.184(d)). Some findings mean permanent removal: chain heated above 1000 °F (1910.184(e)(6)), fiber core wire rope exposed to more than 200 °F (1910.184(f)(3)), and any defective fiber rope sling, since repaired fiber rope slings may not be used (1910.184(h)(6)).
The sling manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks; 1910.184(c) lists further rigging practices, and metal mesh slings have their own removal conditions in 1910.184(g)(9).

sections.title: All slings: inspection, markings and rigging
items: A competent person designated by the employer checked the sling and all fastenings and attachments for damage or defects today, before first use
Marking is affixed to the sling and can be read
Load to be lifted is no more than the manufacturer's recommended safe working load shown on the sling's markings
No damage or defect of any kind is visible on the sling in use
Sling length not shortened with knots, bolts or other makeshift devices
Sling securely attached to the load before lifting
Padding or protection between the sling and every sharp edge of the load
Every employee is clear of the load before lift-off and while it is suspended
No shock loading during the lift

sections.title: Alloy steel chain slings
items: Durable, permanently affixed tag states reach, size, grade and rated capacity
Thorough inspection done at the employer's set interval and no more than 12 months ago
Record of the most recent month of thorough inspection exists for this sling and can be shown on request
No point on any link is below the minimum chain size in Table N-184-1
No cracked or deformed master links, coupling links or other components
Hook has no cracks, its throat at the narrowest spot has not opened over 15% beyond normal, and it is twisted no more than 10 degrees out of the unbent hook's plane
No makeshift links or fasteners formed from bolts or rods
Chain has not been heated above 1000 °F

sections.title: Wire rope slings
items: Legible, permanently affixed manufacturer marking shows safe working load per hitch, the angle it is based on, and leg count on multi-leg slings
Fewer than ten randomly distributed broken wires in any rope lay, and fewer than five in any one strand of a lay
Outside wires have not lost one-third of their original diameter to wear or scraping
No kinking, crushing, bird caging or other distortion
No evidence of heat damage on the rope
A fiber core rope has never been exposed to temperatures above 200 °F
End attachments free of cracks, deformation and wear
Throat not opened past 15% of normal at its narrowest; twist within 10 degrees of the unbent position
No corrosion on the rope or end attachments

sections.title: Synthetic web slings
items: Marking or code shows hitch-by-hitch rated capacities and the web material
No snags, punctures, tears or cuts in the webbing
No melting or charring anywhere on the sling surface
A nylon sling is not used where acids or phenolics are present as fume, vapor, spray, mist or liquid
A polyester or polypropylene sling is not used where caustics are present as fume, vapor, spray, mist or liquid
A web sling with aluminum fittings is kept away from caustics, whatever the form (fumes, mists, vapors, sprays or liquids)
A polyester or nylon sling is not used above 180 °F; a polypropylene sling is not used above 200 °F

sections.title: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings
items: Legible, permanently affixed marking shows rated capacity per hitch and its angle, the fiber type, and leg count on multi-leg slings
No abnormal wear on the rope
No variations in the size or roundness of strands
No distortion of hardware in the sling
Sling is made from new rope and has never been repaired or reconditioned
Used between minus 20 °F and plus 180 °F, or as its manufacturer recommends when outside that range or wet frozen

references: 29 CFR 1910.184: Slings (Part 1910 Subpart N, Materials Handling and Storage)
